writeup: TIC 94125661 is a candidate eclipsing binary star identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry data. The system shows a primary eclipse that dims the star by 25.18% with an orbital period of 3.2293 days. A secondary eclipse was also detected at a signal-to-noise ratio of 6.1 sigma, occurring near orbital phase 0.49, suggesting two stars orbiting each other. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates from the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 52.2. The overall detection significance reaches 239.2 in the Box Least Squares analysis. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate for follow-up study by other observers and instruments.
